Use the model above to solve the following multiplication problem. You do not need to simplify your answer.

$\frac{3}{5}\times \frac{1}{2}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Since we need to multiply by $\frac{1}{2}$, we split the whole into $2$ equal parts horizontally and ensure that $1$ of the parts remains shaded.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14130839/assets/2f06814dd3cbc6990fad45eb05bc77856f0eda54185388d2c1e2795275beadad.png)

From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents $\frac{3}{10}$ of the whole.

Therefore,

$$
\frac{3}{5}\times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{10}.
$$
